description: The Global Groundwater Information System is IGRAC's interactive portal for sharing data and information on groundwater resources worldwide, built on GeoNode. Coverage: global; on 29 September 2026 the GeoNode API listed 1,058 resources, of which 579 datasets, 429 documents and 16 maps; datasets include the Global Groundwater Monitoring Network levels, springs and quality data, the Groundwater Observations Repository, transboundary aquifers of the world (2025), the global managed aquifer recharge (MAR) inventory (2026), groundwater level percentiles used in the WMO State of Global Water Resources reports (2023 to 2025), global aquifer system boundaries and groundwater decline from Jasechko et al. (2024), a global fluoride model, PFAS contamination (2023), the G3P gravity-based groundwater product and national hydrogeological maps such as those of Mali. Format and access: map layers and documents viewable and downloadable through the portal, well and monitoring data downloadable after naming the providers or countries and identifying oneself, and remote queries through Web Map Service and Sensor Observation Service interfaces; free. Licence: set per dataset; among the first 100 datasets from the API, 66 state no licence, 14 are ODbL, and others carry provider-specific or derived terms; the portal's disclaimer and licensing page was not read. Caveats: coverage and update frequency depend on each data provider; some layers are test uploads. Simulation uses: groundwater levels, aquifer boundaries and contamination layers for drinking water supply, drought adaptation studies of infrastructure. Related records: GEMStat water quality (data-unep-gems-water-gemstat-global-water-quality) and the European Soil Data Centre (data-jrc-esdac-european-soil-data-centre).
